title: Strengthening authentication: length/complexity, randomness, MFA
goal_html: Students work through the TOTP algorithm by hand (with a calculator) for one time step, verify their result matches the simulator, and then reason about the security properties that emerge from the algorithm's design. Ties to LO 1.2.C (evaluate stronger authentication: length, randomness, MFA).
steps_html:
1. Pairs open the simulation and read Scenario 1 (fixed key and timestamp). Before entering anything, they write out the algorithm steps on paper: a. Compute the time step: step = floor(t / 30). b. Note the key bytes from the hex string. c. The sim uses a deterministic synthetic HMAC (documented in the legend). Predict the code by working through the JavaScript in the sim (open browser DevTools console and call computeTOTP("0a1b2c3d", 1700000010) to verify). d. Enter the code in the sim and submit.
  2. For Scenario 2 (expired code), both partners predict whether the code will be valid 35 seconds later BEFORE reading the sim feedback. They write their prediction and the reasoning.
  3. For Scenario 4 (replay attack), partners write one paragraph explaining why the 30-second window defeats replay even if the attacker acts within 10 seconds of interception.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "authenticator" (computes what code the app would show), the other is the "server" (checks whether the submitted code matches the current step). Swap for Scenario 3. For the replay scenario, one partner plays the attacker; the other argues why the defense works.
exit_html: Each student submits: (1) the correct TOTP code for Scenario 1 with the algorithm trace showing step, digest concept, and final 6-digit code; (2) one sentence explaining what a time-step window prevents and one sentence describing what it does NOT prevent (real-time phishing relay).
